subject: Administrative Law
question: What is quasi-judicial function? Explain with the help of decided cases.

sections.heading: Introduction
paras: Modern welfare states give wide powers to the executive to regulate social and economic activities. Along with rule-making and pure execution, administrative authorities often decide disputes affecting citizens' rights. Such **adjudicatory functions** performed by non-judicial bodies are called **quasi-judicial functions**. The word 'quasi' means 'as if' or 'similar to', showing that the authority acts like a court without being a regular court.

sections.heading: Meaning and Essentials of Quasi-Judicial Function

points.title: Legal Authority by Statute
points.text: The administrative body or tribunal must derive its power from a valid **statute or statutory rule**. Without **legal authority**, no official can claim to decide legal rights or impose binding liabilities on citizens.

points.title: Determination of Rights
points.text: The authority must be empowered to determine questions affecting the **legal rights** or **civil liabilities** of individuals. Mere preliminary inquiries or policy recommendations that do not finally affect rights are not quasi-judicial.

points.title: Duty to Act Judicially
points.text: There must be an express or implied **duty to act judicially**. This requires the authority to decide objectively based on **evidence and law**, rather than personal whims or administrative expediency.

points.title: Presence of a Lis
points.text: Often there is a **lis**, meaning a dispute between two **opposing parties**, or a contest between a citizen and the department. Even without a formal dispute, a duty to act judicially may arise.

points.title: Observance of Natural Justice
points.text: The authority must follow the **principles of natural justice**, namely the rule against bias (**nemo judex in causa sua**) and the right to a fair hearing (**audi alteram partem**), before passing any adverse order.

sections.heading: Quasi-Judicial vs Administrative and Judicial Functions
paras: A **pure judicial function** is exercised by regular courts strictly bound by technical rules of evidence and procedure. In contrast, a **quasi-judicial authority** is not bound by strict courtroom rules like the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, so long as it follows fairness and **natural justice**.

While a **pure administrative function** is guided mainly by government policy, expediency, and subjective satisfaction, a **quasi-judicial function** demands objective assessment of facts and law. However, modern Indian courts hold that **fairness in action** applies even to administrative decisions having civil consequences.

cases.name: Province of Bombay v. Khushaldas S. Advani (1950)
cases.text: The Supreme Court laid down the classic **four-fold test** for a quasi-judicial act: a body of persons having **legal authority** to determine questions affecting rights of subjects, and having the **duty to act judicially**. Requisitioning property was held administrative on facts.

cases.name: A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India (1969)
cases.text: The Supreme Court held that the dividing line between **administrative** and **quasi-judicial** powers is very thin and gradually disappearing. Even an administrative selection board must follow **natural justice** when its decision affects rights and carries civil consequences.

cases.name: Indian National Congress (I) v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002)
cases.text: The Court clarified that where a statutory authority is required to act **judicially** while deciding a dispute or affecting rights, its function is **quasi-judicial**, even if there is no **lis** between two private parties.

sections.heading: Conclusion
paras: To sum up, **quasi-judicial functions** bridge the gap between pure administration and formal courts, ensuring speedy yet fair justice. Though courts have blurred the strict distinction between administrative and quasi-judicial acts through the doctrine of **fairness**, identifying a function as quasi-judicial remains vital for claiming **certiorari**, reasoned orders, and strict adherence to natural justice.

myth.myth: Only regular courts and judges can perform quasi-judicial functions and pass legally binding orders.
myth.law: **Administrative authorities** and **tribunals** also perform **quasi-judicial functions** when empowered by statute to decide **legal rights** objectively after following natural justice.
myth.source_say: Under Articles 136 and 226 of the Constitution, courts review tribunal and quasi-judicial orders.

quiz.question: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court hold that the dividing line between administrative and quasi-judicial powers is very thin?
options: A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India (1969)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Kharak Singh v. State of UP (1962)
quiz.explain: In **A.K. Kraipak**, the Supreme Court ruled that the boundary between administrative and quasi-judicial powers is blurring, requiring natural justice in both.

case.name: Province of Bombay v. Khushaldas S. Advani (1950)
case.facts: Bombay Government requisitioned a flat under the 1947 Ordinance without hearing the tenant. The tenant challenged it through a writ of certiorari.
case.issue: Whether the government order requisitioning property was a quasi-judicial act amenable to a writ of certiorari.
case.held: The Court held it was an **administrative act** based on subjective satisfaction, so a **writ of certiorari** could not be issued.
case.principle: An act is **quasi-judicial** only when a body with **legal authority** determines rights and has a statutory **duty to act judicially**.

rows.label: Basis of Decision
rows.say: Quasi-judicial decisions rely on objective law and facts, while administrative ones rely on policy.

rows.label: Fair Hearing
rows.say: A hearing is mandatory in quasi-judicial acts, and applies to administrative acts only when civil consequences follow.

rows.label: Writ Remedy
rows.say: Courts issue certiorari against quasi-judicial errors, whereas mandamus compels administrative duties.

rows.label: Reasoned Order
rows.say: Quasi-judicial bodies must pass speaking orders with reasons, unlike routine administrative orders.
